correctness.rationale: For an arbitrary finite loopless quiver and every finite field, (i) direct path-algebra multiplication gives \([x,y]_e=(a_{s(e)}-a_{t(e)})y_e-(b_{s(e)}-b_{t(e)})x_e\); (ii) nonmonochromatic arrows give independent pivots and monochromatic support gives a rescaled graphic incidence matrix of rank \(n-k(S)\); (iii) coefficients \(q^{m-|E_a|}(q-1)^{|S|}\) enumerate all elements without duplication; (iv) rank-nullity yields centralizer orders; (v) maximizing the adjoint rank minimizes monochromatic cycle excess and gives the induced-forest coloring criterion; and (vi) interchanging sums gives commuting pairs \(q^m\sum_{S\subseteq E}(q-1)^{|S|}q^{2k(S)}\). Empty edges, isolated vertices, parallel edges, every characteristic and nonprime finite fields are included. The included exhaustive checker directly verifies eight cases; finite tests only corroborate the general proof.

value.rationale: The theorem exactly classifies the rank of every inner commutator operator across all finite loopless quiver radical-square-zero algebras, including nonisomorphic orientations. This is a natural structural invariant and relates its maximal possible rank to vertex arboricity, an independently motivated graph parameter; q=2 versus q=3 on K5 exhibits a field-order obstruction. The classical Potts identity expresses all commuting-pair counts. It is an infinite all-quiver result, not an arbitrary finite table, isolated computational gain, or renaming of a known special case.
